body: This test will pollute `C:\` and can only succeed once (dir already exists). Please add an `#[ignore]` to restrict it to CI-only or fix that.

Does this really need `canonicalize` at every level or at all? We can be reasonably sure that the first path exists, and each call will do I/O. Both the overrides and cwd should already be canonicalized (`dunce` will just sometimes strip the prefix).

I'd prefer to just strip the prefixes and convert each level directly into a `String`.

> I'd prefer to just strip the prefixes and convert each level directly into a `String`.

This probably boils down to a general design-decision. Personally I prefer using library features ( in this case, for paths and their comparison) over reinventing the wheel. In the end, this is what lead to this bug here since prefix-matching works different for strings and paths. 

Secondly, this mimics how `rustup` does it, so possible edge-cases I don't know about are covered. 

IMO I/O effort is negligible in comparison to the rest of starship or even the rest of the rust-module. 

**Of course if that's preferred I can fix the prefix matching while still using strings and not paths.**

> Both the overrides and cwd should already be canonicalized (dunce will just sometimes strip the prefix).

For the overrides you're probably right, since rustup probably stores the canonicalized path in `settings.yml`.  But when I removed the canonicalization for the overrides, the windows-test failed. How does the `settings.yml` look on windows compared to the tests?

>Personally I prefer using library features ( in this case, for paths and their comparison) over reinventing the wheel.

Aren't this code and rustup itself just creating string keys for each parent and comparing them? I'd prefer not doing canonicalization here, but if you feel strongly about it, you can stay with this approach.

> But when I removed the canonicalization for the overrides, the windows-test failed.

Rustup unconditionally removes the verbatim path prefix. The canonicalization adds back the prefix back to both `current_dir` and the override and makes them match (this code is doing the opposite of rustup).

> Personally I prefer using library features ( in this case, for paths and their comparison) over reinventing the wheel.

By the way: #3414 seems to be doing proper Path-based comparison and should not be too far off.

> > Personally I prefer using library features ( in this case, for paths and their comparison) over reinventing the wheel.
> 
> By the way: #3414 seems to be doing proper Path-based comparison and should not be too far off.

Are you sure this works on windows too? 

To me #3414 looks like it's reverting the windows-specific change you made in #3359, and just comparing a `PathBuf` override with a `Path` cwd.

> Rustup unconditionally removes the verbatim path prefix. The canonicalization adds back the prefix back to both `current_dir` and the override and makes them match (this code is doing the opposite of rustup).

I thought I read the rustup code correctly and mimicked its behaviour. I will check this again.

> Are you sure this works on windows too?

There's room for improvement, but it should work most of the time because the verbatim path prefix is usually stripped by `dunce` now.

Stripping the prefix is still somewhat more correct, because paths that are potentially invalid without the verbatim prefix will not have it stripped by dunce, whereas IIRC rustup is doing it unconditionally.

It would be better to convert the Path to `&str`, strip the prefix and convert it back to `Path` for `Path::starts_with`.
